source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 149: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: treat a calculator call as unnecessary only when the required operation and precision are already safely determined from the prompt; otherwise classify it as justified or abstain rather than infer. Hypothesis: on a preregistered, held-out mix of known-answer, tool-required, ambiguous, and adversarial tasks, a typed stop/no-tool gate will reduce unnecessary-call rate and median trajectory length and tool latency, while final-correctness lower confidence bound is no more than 1 percentage point below the ungated policy. Intervention: add an explicit decision state (stop, answer, calculator-needed, or clarify), require a parseable expression and unit/precision check before calling, cap retries at two, validate the returned value and units against the request, and fall back to a transparent uncertainty/clarification response on timeout, malformed, unavailable, or inconsistent output. Do not expose private data to the tool or bypass authorization. Measure per request: unnecessary-call rate, justified-call recall, tool success/validation rate, final correctness, trajectory length, recovery rate after tool failure, tool latency in milliseconds, queue/timeouts, and abstention/clarification rate, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and slice results. Include no-tool, tool-required, precision-boundary, ambiguous, malformed, wrong-result, timeout, duplicate-call, retry-loop, and adversarial-output tests. Use randomized paired assignment with identical prompts, model/configuration, tool version, and seeds where applicable; keep tuning separate from the held-out set and compare correctness, call rate, latency, cost, and calibration. Confounders include prompt difficulty, answer length, model drift, tool load, cache state, retry policy, and changing arrival mix; stratify or log them. Canary gradually, alert on correctness, unsafe disclosure, tail latency, or failure-recovery regressions, and roll back the gate/reward change if predefined bounds are crossed. A preference/reward signal may favor correct minimal trajectories, but must be capped and never reward abstention when a tool is required.
risks: A gate can suppress a necessary calculation or create false confidence at precision and unit boundaries.
Call-rate gains can be confounded by workload mix, tool load, cache state, or reward-induced abstention.
